kpis.sub: 2026/FY27 CAPEX — TOP-5 HYPERSCALERS; GOOGL & MSFT HELD, DID NOT RAISE
kpis.label: Amazon (~$220B, guide maintained), Alphabet ($195–205B reference range; Q3 capex $51.4B, +114%, free cash flow −$9.1B), Microsoft (~$175B CY2026 after an accounting change that lengthens data-center/building useful lives from 15 to 25 years and shifts some leases to operating; Q3 capex $39.4B, +103%), Meta ($135–145B; Q3 $34.9B, FCF −$2.1B) and Oracle (S&P models $90–95B FY2027). CNBC (Oct 29) headlined that Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecasts. Amazon's reported Q3 spend was ~$76B per a secondary source, trailing-12-month free cash flow −$42.4B. Consensus has 2026 tech-infrastructure capex near $790B and ~$1.2T in 2027. The binding constraint is financing: Goldman projects hyperscaler debt issuance rising from ~$250B in 2026 to ~$420B in 2027, with ~35% of 2027 capex debt-funded

kpis.sub: ANTHROPIC PUBLIC S-1 FILED OCT 26; OPENAI CUT RAISE TO $20B
kpis.label: Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 on Oct 26 (Nasdaq, ticker ANT, 22 underwriters led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley per a Leverage Shares summary of the filing — an interested party; EDGAR not independently checked). No price range or share count yet. WSJ (Oct 26) says it could raise $100B+ at $1.5–2T with a listing targeted for the week of Nov 16; the roadshow cannot start until ~15 days after the public filing (~Nov 10). Filing figures: FY2025 revenue $4.6B; H1 2026 revenue $16.3B (vs $1.2B in H1 2025) and a net loss of $80.7B, of which $72.4B is non-cash fair-value changes. Run-rate was reported above $65B in late July. Last private mark $965B (May). Blackstone has warned Anthropic may not get an investment-grade rating after IPO. OpenAI: the FT (Nov 1) says its raise is now $20B at $1.25T, down from $30B at $1.4T (CNBC on Oct 22 had 'up to $30B at $1.25T pre-money'); not reported closed. All press reports, subject to change

kpis.sub: NASDAQ OCT 30; ALPHABET, AMAZON, INTEL SOLD OFF ON EARNINGS

Earnings reactions were split: Microsoft rose ~3–4% after hours on Azure +48% to $33.2B (revenue $92.3B, +19%); Alphabet fell ~8–13% depending on source (revenue $127.6B, EPS $2.12 vs ~$3.00 expected on an $8.7B equity-investment loss, but Google Cloud +103% to $30.7B); Amazon fell ~4% in the session and ~6% after hours (AWS +39% to $46B, fastest in nearly five years, record 13.9% operating margin, but TTM free cash flow −$42.4B); Intel fell nearly 30% on a weak Q4 outlook. bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: The industry has committed an estimated $3–4T to AI infrastructure against an annualized return requirement of roughly $600–800B in new profit, while AI-attributable revenue runs an estimated $50–150B a year. Consensus tech-infrastructure capex is ~$790B in 2026 and ~$1.2T in 2027; Gartner (Oct 14) warned that $3.5T+ of AI infrastructure spending could face impairment by 2030. OpenAI's ~$50B run-rate and a lower-priced $1.25T raise, plus Anthropic's slowdown to ~+45–50% QoQ ($16.8B Q3), show the two largest buyers of compute growing slower than the market modeled. Counterpoint: Anthropic is reportedly cash-flow positive at an 85% gross margin, TSMC guided Q4 more than $4B above Street, Lam posted record revenue (+54%) and ASML says customers want 2029–2030 tools — Huang and Dan Ives frame it as a financing issue, not a demand issue. This week's prints sharpened the cash-flow side: Alphabet's Q3 free cash flow was −$9.1B, Amazon's trailing-12-month FCF −$42.4B, Meta's first negative FCF quarter since 2012 — spending is now outrunning internally generated cash at three of five hyperscalers.

bear_case.title: AI's own architects sound the alarm
bear_case.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published "We Must Pace the Frontier" on Sept 12, arguing AI capability growth has accelerated "drastically faster" since summer 2026 — driven mainly by AI's growing ability to build the next generation of AI — and proposing independent safety evaluation, inter-lab coordination and international cooperation. OpenAI's Sam Altman and DeepMind's Demis Hassabis publicly backed the call; days later Palantir's Alex Karp went further, telling CNBC that frontier labs may need to be nationalized over "unlimited risk." The market reaction was real — chip names sold off while Meta, Alphabet and Microsoft rose — but skeptics note that a company mid-prep for a ~$2T IPO calling for the industry to slow down is also a moat-building and regulatory-capture argument, not purely an act of altruism.

bear_case.title: Rates and financing are now the transmission mechanism
bear_case.description: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 in Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair, with two dissents in favor of a hike (per headlines); futures priced meaningful odds of a December hike before the meeting. The 10-year is near 4.9–5.0%. The Nasdaq fell 2.9% on Oct 30 for its worst month since March 2025. The bond market is skeptical: on Oct 27 Nvidia's 2060 note traded below 64 cents on the dollar, Oracle's 2065 below 73, Meta's 2064 below 77 and CoreWeave's 2031 below 80 (Motley Fool; long-dated prices partly reflect rates). Goldman expects hyperscaler issuance to rise from ~$250B in 2026 to ~$420B in 2027, with ~35% of 2027 capex debt-funded; tech has already issued nearly $500B this year. CDS on Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle hit their highest since 2021 (WSJ), CoreWeave saw record October put volume and Jump Trading launched a derivatives desk on chip-rental prices — hedging demand is real, though WSJ notes it remains small relative to the AI investment boom.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments off hyperscaler balance sheets, and a Nikkei Asia analysis of SEC filings counts ~$1.35T of hyperscaler balance-sheet debt alongside ~$1.65T of off-balance-sheet commitments. The RBA's Oct 1 Financial Stability Review put obligations via SPVs and vendor financing at US$1–1.5T on 20–30 year debt against hardware of 'uncertain economic lives'. Anthropic's leaked S-1 adds $518B of compute commitments, ~80% non-cancellable or take-or-pay. Forbes (Oct 22) puts 2026 AI-related debt issuance above $460–500B; Meta's $27.3B Hyperion bond has traded down to ~91 cents and the data-center high-yield index to ~$95. AI debt is now ~10% of large investment-grade bond ETFs (from 7%). Oracle remains the starkest case (BBB-, RPO $664B vs net debt ~$132B, ~$40B planned raise). Counterpoint: the RBA notes aggregate leverage remains contained and hyperscalers' balance sheets are the strongest in corporate history.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: The BIS (Bulletin 137, Oct 1) found 55.2% of investment value into 1,246 AI-supply-chain firms came from other AI firms, 28.7% of AI firms' invested value went to other AI firms, and 46.4% of AI-to-AI deal value involved supply-chain relationships. Broadcom is reportedly arranging $50B+ of financing for OpenAI's custom chips, Anthropic's S-1 shows ~$161B of Broadcom equipment-lease contracts, Nvidia is in talks to anchor up to $10B of Anthropic's IPO, and its DSX Pod design aims to make GPU clusters bankable collateral. Burry calls Nvidia's revenue 'majority circularly financed'; Nvidia's CDS hit a record ~101bp. Counterpoint: the BIS frames this as a feature of a young supply chain rather than proof of systemic risk, and Anthropic's reported adjusted operating profit suggests at least one lab can fund itself.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years; Burry argues replacement cycles are really 2–3 years, understating depreciation by ~$176B across 2026–2028 and inflating Oracle's earnings by ~27% and Meta's by ~21%. Forbes (Oct 22) notes GPUs may be obsolete within 3–5 years while debt is secured against them. Meta's negative Q3 free cash flow on $34.9B of quarterly capex puts the depreciation wall in view. Bull evidence: CoreWeave's CEO says H100 capacity was rebooked at ~95% of the original contract price and Nvidia says A100s are rented through 2029. Bear evidence: that is rental pricing for the best-contracted capacity, not proof the economic life of the whole installed base is 5–6 years. CoreWeave (bonds 14–16%, shares −15% Oct 14–15 and −10% Oct 22) is the live stress test. Microsoft's Oct 28 change extending data-center and building useful lives from 15 to 25 years (and moving some leases from finance to operating) lowers reported capex and flatters earnings; it concerns structures rather than GPUs, but critics will read it alongside the 5–6 year server schedules.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Layoffs.fyi's tracker showed 128,536 tech workers cut across 299 companies in 2026 through Sept 10 (not refreshed this edition) — already exceeding all of 2025 — while a broader tracker (SkillSyncer, different methodology) counts 210,741 workers across 383 layoff events through Sept 20. xAI itself cut roughly 500 data-annotation staff (a third of that team) on Sept 12 as part of a stated pivot to "specialist AI tutors." The juxtaposition — record infrastructure spend, record layoffs, and AI labs restructuring their own workforces — keeps fueling the argument that AI economics lean partly on cost-cutting elsewhere, not purely on AI revenue.

bear_case.title: Bull evidence: demand is still accelerating
bear_case.description: Against the bear case: Azure grew 48% (accelerating), AWS 39% (fastest in nearly five years, with management guiding above 40% for 2027–28), and Google Cloud 103% at a 36% operating margin. Nvidia B300 rental rates are up ~56% this year to $7.56/hour, which argues GPUs are not yet commoditizing; TSMC guided Q4 more than $4B above Street; ASML's orders stretch toward 2030; and Anthropic's filing shows H1 2026 revenue of $16.3B versus $1.2B a year earlier, with the lab reportedly profitable before stock compensation. Capex guides at Alphabet and Microsoft were held rather than raised. The debate is increasingly about who funds the buildout and at what cost of capital, not whether customers will use the compute. AI startups also drew a record $102B (64%) of Q3's $159B global venture total, with 27 rounds of $1B+ (Crunchbase), though that concentration is itself a bear point.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took over 40% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total, and AI took 86% of all US venture dollars in H1 per PitchBook), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage and quantum sentiment at once. NVIDIA now sits at the center of deals spanning chips (TSMC, Broadcom), model hosting (Hugging Face), enterprise software (Palantir) and a potential anchor stake in Anthropic's IPO — a single company's balance sheet increasingly touches nearly every layer of this page, even as customers like Anthropic simultaneously build Google TPU alternatives. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters (TSMC, ASML, Lam) — some strategists call the bear case premature given actual demand signals; this week software and security names (Zscaler +23%, CrowdStrike +13%) rallied as capital rotated within tech. Crunchbase puts Q3 2026 global venture at $159B (−25% vs Q2), with AI taking 64% ($102B) and a record 27 billion-dollar rounds (Databricks and SSI $5B each; Crusoe, Moonshot AI and Mistral $3B+) — fewer, bigger bets.

etfs.summary: The silicon layer: NVDA/TSM/AVGO-heavy. Chips were hit by the Oct 22 rout (SOX −6.7%) and the Oct 30 Nasdaq drop (−2.9%) with Intel down ~30% on guidance; the weekly SOX/SMH move and YTD were not verified this week. Heaviest exposure to the Nvidia-customer financing loop

etfs.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence & Tech
etfs.summary: Broad AI beneficiaries across the stack; this week's cloud-growth prints (Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud +103%) helped Microsoft but Alphabet and Amazon fell. Earlier ~+20% YTD figure is stale and not re-verified — likely lower now

etfs.name: Invesco Nasdaq-100
etfs.summary: The de-facto AI mega-cap index: the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9% on Oct 30 for its worst month since March 2025, with Alphabet and Amazon the earnings-day drags. Cheapest exposure (0.18% fee vs SMH's 0.35%) and lowest volatility of the three, but with the most overlap with everything else you own; price and YTD not re-verified

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: TSMC
positions.note: Least circularly-financed name here: record Q3 (revenue $46.7B, +41%; profit +69%) and a Q4 guide >$4B above Street, and this week's Azure +48%, AWS +39% and Google Cloud +103% prints all feed its order book.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: Google Cloud +103% to $30.7B at a 36% margin and TPU demand (3.5GW for Anthropic) are the strongest evidence on the page, but the EPS miss, −$9.1B free cash flow and an ~8–13% post-earnings drop show the price no longer forgives spending. Also appears in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Amazon
positions.note: AWS +39% (fastest in nearly five years) and a record 13.9% operating margin support the payback thesis, but trailing-12-month free cash flow of −$42.4B and a ~6% post-earnings drop leave little room if financing tightens.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Q3 guide ~$108B at ~75% margin and B300 rental rates +56% YTD show demand, but at ~$205 (~16% below its $243 record) it is exposed to customer funding strain — OpenAI's raise cut to $20B, Nvidia's 2060 bond under 64 cents. Also sits in the Quantum, Robotics and AI Biotech sleeves — don't double-count.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: Azure +48% (accelerating) and $18.6B free cash flow are the best cash-backed AI print this week, though the ~$175B capex outlook reflects an accounting change, not restraint, and OpenAI exposure remains. Also in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.note: Growth rests on two cash-burning labs (~$161B of Anthropic lease contracts, $50B+ of financing for OpenAI chips), and OpenAI's raise being cut to $20B at $1.25T tests that funding; Anthropic's IPO is the offsetting upside.

positions.name: AMD
positions.note: Tied to OpenAI's 6GW GPU deal while OpenAI's raise shrinks, and it reports Nov 3 after falling 8.1% on Oct 22 — wait for the print.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.note: 5-year CDS at records (~263bp on Oct 14, widening by more than a point in October), its 2065 bond below 73 cents on Oct 27, RPO of $664B against ~$132B net debt and a BBB- rating make it the weakest balance sheet on the page.

positions.name: CoreWeave
positions.note: Record October put volume, bonds yielding 14–16% on ~$46–50B of net debt, CDS near 1,000–1,200bp and a 2031 bond under 80 cents make it the cleanest read on AI credit stress and a bet on GPU residual values.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: Very high multiple with little cushion in a Nasdaq worst-month tape (−2.9% on Oct 30); Q3 results due Nov 2 after the close (guide ~$2.16B, ~+83%) are the test.

positions.name: Meta
positions.note: Q3 free cash flow turned negative (−$2.1B) on $34.9B of capex, the 2026 range sits at $135–145B and its CDS hit a record ~115bp on Oct 22; legal costs add drag.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: ~13% growth versus triple-digit AI-native peers; software was hit in the Oct 16 selloff and agents must prove a tailwind to RPA, not a replacement.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: AI thesis rests on Nvidia dependence and xAI capex of $15.8B in Q2; its CDS hit a record ~203bp in mid-October and frontier-challenger economics remain unproven.
